opp_002:n1.prompt:
You are helping me onboard a new 1099 contractor into our payroll system, {{vendor}}, so they can be paid and receive a 1099 at year-end. 

First, ask me for any of the following if not already provided: the contractor's full legal name, email address, country/state of residence, start date, payment rate and currency, payment frequency (e.g., per project, hourly, monthly), and the {{vendor}} workspace/account identifier if we have multiple.

Once you have these details, use your configured credentials to access {{vendor}}'s API (or dashboard if API access is unavailable) and create the contractor's contract record. If {{vendor}} exposes a documented endpoint for creating a contractor contract (for example, a POST call to a '/rest/contracts' style endpoint), use it; otherwise, complete the equivalent steps through the {{vendor}} dashboard, filling in the same fields (name, contact info, country, compensation terms, payment schedule, and contract start date).

After creating the record, verify it was successfully saved by retrieving or viewing the contractor's profile in {{vendor}} and confirming the name, rate, and country match what I provided.

Done looks like: the contractor exists as an active record in {{vendor}} with correct compensation and identifying details, ready for payment and 1099 tracking at year-end.

Report back to me with: (1) confirmation the contractor record was created, (2) the contractor's name and ID or profile link in {{vendor}}, (3) the compensation and payment terms as entered, and (4) any fields {{vendor}} required that I hadn't provided, so I can supply them.

opp_002:n2.prompt: You are helping me complete step opp_002:n2 in onboarding a new 1099 contractor: getting the contractor to submit their own W-9 and bank/direct-deposit details through our payroll system. Please ask me for anything you need: the contractor's full name and email address, and confirmation of which payroll platform we use (e.g., Gusto, QuickBooks Payroll, Rippling, etc.) since I already have configured credentials for it. Then: 1) Log into our payroll platform using my configured credentials and locate the contractor-onboarding or 'add contractor' flow. 2) Create the contractor record with the name/email I gave you, and trigger the platform's standard invitation so the contractor receives a self-service link to submit their W-9 tax information and bank account details directly. 3) Confirm the invitation was sent successfully and note the contractor's status (e.g., 'invited', 'pending'). Because only the contractor holds their own SSN/EIN and banking details, actually filling out and submitting the W-9 and bank form remains a human step that only the contractor can perform on their own timeline — you cannot do this for them. Your job is to prepare and send the invite, then periodically check (poll) the platform for a status change to 'completed' or 'verified.' Report back to me with: the date you sent the invite, the contractor's current status each time you check, and a clear alert once the status shows the W-9 and bank details have been submitted so we can proceed to the next onboarding step.

opp_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me verify that a 1099 contractor is fully payable in {{vendor}} (our payroll platform) before we run their next payment.

If you don't already have it, ask me for: the contractor's full name or email as entered in {{vendor}}, and our company/account identifier in {{vendor}} if needed to disambiguate.

Using our configured credentials, please:
1. Look up the contractor's record in {{vendor}} and confirm whether a completed W-9 is on file (status, and whether it's signed/submitted vs. still pending).
2. Confirm a valid payment method is set up for them (e.g., bank account/direct deposit or other supported method), and that it's in an active, usable state (not pending verification or failed).
3. If {{vendor}} exposes an API for validating contractor payment readiness, use it to run a preview/validation check against this contractor for the next contractor payment group, and capture any blockers or errors it returns (e.g., missing W-9, missing bank details, unverified account).
4. If either the W-9 or payment method is missing or incomplete, do not attempt to fix it yourself — instead note exactly what's missing and, if {{vendor}} supports sending a self-serve reminder or document request to the contractor, prepare that reminder (with the right recipient and document type) but do not send it without my confirmation.

Done looks like: you have a clear yes/no on both W-9 status and payment method status, plus any validation output from {{vendor}} showing whether this contractor is currently clear to be paid.

Report back to me with: (a) W-9 status, (b) payment method status, (c) any blockers or validation errors returned by {{vendor}}, and (d) a drafted reminder message if something is missing, so I can review before anything is sent. Do not send communications or submit payments on my behalf — flag anything needing my approval and stop for human sign-off.
